consolation

/kon-suh-LAY-shun/ - the stress falls on LAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Consolation means comfort offered or found after a loss or disappointment.

When the tour was canceled, the band's consolation was the bootleg tapes fans mailed from the three shows that happened.

Example

The observatory's forty-year search ended a month too late: a rival team announced the comet first. For weeks the loss sat where the old astronomer's life's work had been. Then he read the rival paper properly and found the footnote — thanks to his survey maps, without which, it said, nothing would have been found at all. He pinned that page, not the award list, above his desk.

Consolation is the exact word for that footnote, because consolation means comfort offered or found after a loss or disappointment — it does not undo the loss, it makes the loss livable. Reassurance calms a fear before the verdict; consolation arrives after, when the verdict has gone the other way.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

solace: Solace is consolation's quieter twin — comfort found as much as given, often sought alone in books, hills, or long walks. Consolation more often arrives from outside, after the loss: a word, a footnote, a prize that makes the thing bearable. You go looking for solace; consolation is handed to you.

comfort: Comfort is the broadest word for easing pain of any kind or size — a blanket, a friend, a warm meal all give comfort, loss or no loss. Consolation is comfort with one particular timing: it follows a loss or disappointment, and its work is making that loss bearable.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

torment: pain deliberately renewed

aggravation: making the hurt worse

Where it sits · how much of the hurt it removes — sympathy → consolation → cure

sympathy vs. consolation: Sympathy is far milder than consolation — it only says I see that it hurts and stands beside the loss without easing it, while consolation actually lightens what the loss weighs.

cure vs. consolation: A cure goes further than consolation — consolation makes a loss livable; a cure takes the loss away entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: thoroughly (an intensifier)

Root — sol

Root — sol: to soothe (Latin solari)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act of

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (thoroughly) + sol- (to soothe) + -ation (the act of) = the act of soothing through and through. The same sol- sits inside solace; consolation is that comfort delivered after the blow has landed.

Use the root in a new word: console

Use the root in a new word: console: To console someone — stress on the second syllable — is to bring them this very comfort: the verb folded inside the noun.
